span.p:
pmCode PM_NNNNNN is the unique business key (uk_pm_code);
it is the only uniqueness the DB enforces — (type, label)
deliberately repeats.
inventoryNumber is a per-type 1..N counter, but only manual
create mints it (max plus 1 under a per-type advisory lock,
ignoring any client value); the importer keeps the sheet's own.
removedAt set means soft-trashed.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
A catalog row, not a Java enum, so a new tape
format needs no redeploy. The nine defaults are
UI autofill only — nothing server-side copies them
onto a record. Renaming name does NOT rewrite
existing physical_media rows, which is why the link
above is 0..1: a renamed type orphans its rows.
Delete is refused while any row still uses the name.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
Maximally lenient, and no dedupe: every non-empty
sheet row becomes a new record with its own pmCode.
A row that fails to persist is retried with stripped
fields before it counts as skipped. Each row runs in
its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction, so one bad row
cannot roll back the batch. One IMPORT audit entry
per batch, not per row.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
/api/physical-media: reads need physical_media:read,
writes need :create / :update / :remove / :import.
/api/admin/physical-media (trash, restore, purge) is
gated by the single authority physical_media:delete.
/api/physical-media/types reads on :read, writes on
:type_manage.
